Definition: Does the government maintain a digital address register?
Comments: Ghana has an official national digital addressing system (GhanaPostGPS) that provides unique digital addresses across the country, indicating a nationwide digital address register/system is deployed.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Peer-reviewed 2024 evaluation and the official platform confirm GhanaPostGPS covers the entire country (5x5m grid nationwide) since 2017. Note: adoption/usage is separately weak (a 2025-26 review says under 20% of Ghanaians actively use their address), but that concerns uptake, not whether the register/system exists, so Status remains 5.

Definition: Is the register integrated with the address register?
Comments: ORC service information instructs filers to provide an ‘accurate digital address’ (GhanaPostGPS-style) in filing forms, suggesting planned/operational use of standardized digital addresses, but no evidence of database-level integration with the address register was found.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed from Planned to Partially integrated. A GhanaPostGPS digital address has been a mandatory field for business registration since March 2019 (Companies Act 2019, s.13(2)) and still is in the current (2025) ORC registration form; a 2019 ministerial statement describes the Ghana Post system as already integrated with ORC/GRA/SSNIT/MMDA systems. This is beyond 'planned', though no evidence of a live API-level validation against the address database was found, so 'fully integrated' is not supported.

Definition: Is the register integrated with the national ID system?
Comments: The Ghana CRVS digitization user-stories document describes automated messaging between the civil registration system and the NIA system (e.g., sending new birth notification to NIA and receiving a generated PIN to update the birth record), indicating integration with national ID is being implemented (under development).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed from Under development to Partially integrated. The 'Ghana Card Number at Birth' system, launched March 2024, provides automated, real-time exchange between health facilities, the Births and Deaths Registry and the National Identification Authority so newborns receive a Ghana Card number linked to their birth record. This is a functioning, if not yet universal, technical integration (it covers new births going forward, with catch-up registration for older children ongoing in 2026), replacing the stale 2017 source.

Definition: Are all non-citizens allowed to be included in the register?
Comments: BDR’s 2022 statistical report includes analysis of non-Ghanaian parents (e.g., ‘non-Ghanaian fathers’), implying non-citizens can be recorded in civil registration records associated with births in Ghana; this indicates broad inclusion beyond only permanent residents, but explicit ‘all non-citizens’ language wasn’t located.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed, with stronger sourcing. The Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 2020 (Act 1027) requires registration of every birth occurring in Ghana regardless of nationality, citizenship, residency or refugee/asylum status, and a peer-reviewed statelessness study confirms UNHCR/Ghana Refugee Board practice of securing birth certificates for refugee children. This is a clearer, more authoritative basis for 'All included' than the original single statistical report.

Definition: What proportion of the population does the register cover?
Comments: BDR’s Statistical Report on Birth Registration states national birth registration coverage of 92.7% for 2022, which is used as a proxy for CRVS uptake (>89%).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed from >89% to 70-89%. UNICEF's Ghana country page states birth registration completeness has 'increased to around 70 per cent' and a 2025 peer-reviewed review puts under-5 completeness at approximately 70% as of 2021, consistent with historical urban rates around 79-80%. This is well corroborated across two independent, more authoritative sources and does not support the BDR's own 92.7% figure, which appears to use a different or narrower measurement basis. Banded to 70-89%.

Definition: Is the register integrated with the national ID system?
Comments: Electoral Commission states a voter must present a valid National ID Card (“Ghana Card”) or passport (or guarantor form) to register, demonstrating partial integration/use of national ID for voter registration but not evidence of full database linkage.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed from Partially integrated to Under development. The Ghana Card is only one of several accepted proofs of identity (alongside a passport or a two-person guarantor system); in the 2023 registration exercise over 60% of new registrants used the guarantor route rather than the Ghana Card, and Parliament rejected the EC's 2023 attempt to make the Ghana Card the sole/mandatory identity document. No evidence was found of a technical (API or biometric deduplication) link between the EC's voter database and the NIA's Ghana Card database; legislative moves to require this are still pending. This is better described as under development than partially integrated.

Definition: What proportion of the electorate does the register cover?
Comments: IFES Election Guide reports 18,774,195 registered voters for Ghana’s 2024 presidential election; relative to adult population/eligible electorate this implies high coverage but not necessarily >89%, so coded 70–89%.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: HUMAN REVIEW SUGGESTED — likely upward revision to >89%. The EC's certified 2024 register lists 18,774,159 voters. Ghana Statistical Service's 2021 census puts the 18+ population share at 58.2%, and its 2024 population projection at approximately 33.0 million, implying an adult population of roughly 19.1-19.2 million — giving registered-voter coverage of about 98%, i.e. band >89% rather than 70-89%. Flagged for human review rather than asserted outright because voter rolls commonly retain deceased/duplicate entrants that inflate the ratio, and 'electorate' definitions (citizens abroad, prisoners) may not exactly match the census denominator.

Definition: Does the government maintain a separate cadastral register?
Comments: Lands Commission documentation on digitization references title plan preparation, digitized maps, and creation of a national cadastre as part of digital transformation (systems like GELIS/ELIS), indicating a cadastral component is being deployed digitally, but not proven fully nationwide.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed from Partially deployed to Under development. Ghana does not maintain a clearly separate, nationally deployed cadastral register distinct from its deeds/title system; the Survey and Mapping Division undertakes cadastral survey within the unified Lands Commission structure. A June 2026 investigative report finds the World Bank-backed Ghana Digital Acceleration Project stalled since February 2025 and an $85m digitisation deal with PDB Ghana still unsigned as of 2026, and a 2024 peer-reviewed case study of Accra's system finds it 'at the beginning of a comprehensive learning and development curve' with manual processes still coexisting with digital ones. This fresher evidence supports 'under development' rather than 'partially deployed'.
